name: WW2 bullet cryptogram, Tuscany
date: 8/13/44 (13 August 1944, as dated on the note itself)
ciphertext_source: Cipherbrain post 44 (Schmeh 2017, sources/schmeh/posts/44-bullet.txt), 'A hidden and encrypted message' section, transcribed by Schmeh from the scan: 'QM / CBFUK YYEVO ZILOO / ZVNCW JKQRS AWBYZ / UGYTZ WYBAT RSUA / 605YZ/FF'. Originally reported by the news portal SPLOID (January 2015), found by an Italian metal detectorist in a German bullet casing in southern Tuscany. Schmeh: 'The first (QM) and the last line (605YZ/FF) probably contain some meta information. The main part of the message has 44 letters.'
alphabet: Latin capitals A-Z, main body 44 letters in nine 5-letter groups (last group 4 letters), plus a 2-letter header (QM) and an alphanumeric footer (605YZ/FF) treated as metadata, not part of the enciphered body

constraints.dated: 8/13/44, probably written by an Allied soldier during the 1944 liberation of Tuscany from German occupation
constraints.form: 5-letter groups (the classic WW2 field-cipher group format), all-letter (no digits within the body, unlike Slidex which mixes letters and digits)
constraints.rejected_solution: a forum poster (via the SPLOID article) proposed: 'THEY THROW GRENADES WE PULL PINS AND THROW BACK' for the 5-letter groups and 'NOTIFY REINFORCEMENTS STAND DOWN - NOT NEEDED' for the final code; Schmeh rejects this explicitly -- no method was shown for how the decryption works, and the claimed plaintext ('the Germans really so stupid?', 'why would a soldier write down such a message, encrypt it and hide it in a bullet?') does not hold up under scrutiny
constraints.candidate_ciphers: Schmeh's own guess is a British or American field cipher (hand-usable, no heavy machine); notes Slidex mixes letters and digits (the body here is letters-only, an argument against Slidex specifically); mentions the M-209 (US) as the most popular contemporary field-cipher machine, plus the older M-94/M-138 as backup devices, without committing to any one

cheap_tests_in_order: 1. Test the rejected forum 'solution' properly and mechanically: attempt to reconstruct any cipher method (Vigenere-family, simple substitution, M-209-style) that actually maps CBFUK YYEVO ZILOO ZVNCW JKQRS AWBYZ UGYTZ WYBAT RSUA to THEYTHROWGRENADESWEPULLPINSANDTHROWBACK under some key; if none exists this closes that claim rather than leaving Schmeh's rejection as prose-only. Cost $1, Sonnet.

2. Simple Vigenere/Caesar-family search with short keys (1-8 letters, including QM and 605YZ/FF read as possible indicator/key material) against an English-military-vocabulary crib list (GRENADE, PIN, REINFORCEMENT, PULL, THROW), judged with a matched control: an English plaintext of N=44 enciphered the same way, same solver, several seeds. At N=44 expect this control itself to read only partially (CLAUDE.md's harry-caroline lesson: small N gives a weak control) -- report both numbers regardless. Cost $1-2.

3. Index-of-coincidence test on the 44-letter body to distinguish monoalphabetic from polyalphabetic before committing to a specific family, matched control: English plaintext N=44 under each candidate family. Cost under $1.
matched_control: not yet run; test 2 above names the design (English plaintext, N=44, same cipher family, same solver); flagged in advance that N=44 is small enough that even a correct method's control may read only partially

1.method: specs/cheap-tests/bullet-tuscany-1944/run_test1.py -- length check (44 cipher letters vs 39 claimed-plaintext letters, decisive on its own for length-preserving families), then a 6-offset scan of every contiguous 39-letter window of the cipher body against the claimed plaintext under Vigenere, Beaufort, variant Beaufort (derived keystream scored for periodicity, periods 1-20) and simple substitution (cipher-to-plaintext mapping consistency/injectivity), with a matched control: the same claimed plaintext enciphered under a real random key of each family (3 seeds), identical script run on the result
1.target_verdict: length mismatch 44 vs 39 (diff 5) rules out a full-body mapping under any of these length-preserving families outright. Fallback 6-offset scan: best periodicity score any offset/family 0.564-0.590 (Vigenere/variant Beaufort 0.590, Beaufort 0.564), all from the degenerate high-period end (period 20, ~2 samples/residue class); at short periods 1-7, where a real key would plausibly sit, target scores only 0.08-0.31, near chance. MASC: minimum 37 of 39 cipher-plaintext pairs violate consistency/injectivity at the best offset (39 at the worst).
1.control_verdict: control (3 seeds) cleanly recovers its planted key for every polyalphabetic family: recovered score 1.0, true period found at all 3 seeds. MASC control: 0 violations, all 3 seeds.
1.conclusion: no key of Vigenere, Beaufort, variant Beaufort or simple substitution maps the 44-letter cipher body to the forum-claimed plaintext; the method demonstrably works (control recovers cleanly) so the target's failure is not a broken test. M-209-style check subsumed by the Beaufort scan (periods 1-20 covers the 'at minimum fixed-period' bar); 39-44 derived letters are too few to test the M-209's own pin/lug structure, not pursued further. Closes the rejected forum claim mechanically per the brief; does not test other cipher families against an undetermined plaintext. Test 2 not run (brief: run test 1 only).

value: medium: a datable, single-author military message with a plausible real-world context (unlike several purely mysterious items in this batch), a named and explicitly rejected false solution to avoid repeating, and a short named list of candidate cipher families (Slidex ruled out by letters-only form, M-209/M-94/M-138 as live candidates) to try in order
status_25_Sept_2026: open; 'a forum solution without a method, rejected by Schmeh' per the survey row; no accepted solution as of the 2017 post
schema_note: cheap_tests_in_order are proposals (rule 10: an approach is not a claim); a test actually run goes under cheap_test_done with its control. The header (QM) and footer (605YZ/FF) are kept separate from the 44-letter body per Schmeh's own reading ('probably contain some meta information') and are not folded into the judge's letter count.
